headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow exposure: Haystack can ingest MCP/REST content and RisingWave is a non-egress data engine, but no shared workspace or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack explicitly calls REST APIs and MCP servers and has broad network egress, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content. RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented output-verification boundary here, so if its outputs are bridged into Haystack via MCP or files, prompt injection is plausible. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are copied into Haystack prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP server or file bridge is configured between the pair, attacker-controlled content can steer Haystack.
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted content.
Add a strict allowlist for Haystack tool inputs.
Insert a content-sanitization step before any Haystack prompt assembly.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all RisingWave-to-Haystack payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints, while RisingWave is a data-engineering system that may process shared datasets. If both are pointed at the same workspace or data source, Haystack can transmit copied content off-box. RisingWave itself shows no egress, so the leakage risk is one-sided but still plausible in default deployments with shared data access.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or dataset, Haystack may exfiltrate copied contents via outbound API calls.
IF sensitive records are routed through Haystack prompts, they can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Restrict Haystack to non-sensitive indexes.
Place Haystack behind an egress allowlist.
Separate datasets so RisingWave and Haystack do not share raw inputs.
Turn off any connector that forwards file contents to external APIs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP/REST interfaces, but RisingWave is marked runnable false and has no documented write surfaces or mutable scopes here. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main uncertainty is missing concurrency and storage details, so I choose low rather than none because a shared mutable backend is not ruled out.
conditions: IF both are wired to the same mutable backend, concurrent updates could conflict.
IF RisingWave is deployed with an external writable sink not shown here, overlap increases.
mitigations: Avoid sharing writable databases between the two agents.
Serialize any writes through one orchestrator.
Use separate service accounts for each system.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can surface retrieved content, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that may feed structured outputs downstream. If RisingWave results are treated as authoritative by Haystack or vice versa, errors can cascade into user-facing answers or pipelines. No verification boundary is documented, so the interaction is inferred and not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are inserted into Haystack retrieval context without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Haystack-generated summaries are used as operational inputs, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require a validation step before Haystack consumes RisingWave outputs.
Mark all cross-agent outputs as untrusted by default.
Add schema checks on structured data before ingestion.
Review a sample of cross-agent outputs daily.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between systems.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only Haystack lists anonymous usage statistics among touched data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to telemetry and any operator-chosen data flows. I cite only Haystack because RisingWave has no compliance-specific fields here.
conditions: IF anonymous usage statistics are collected in a regulated environment, telemetry handling must be reviewed.
IF operators route regulated data through Haystack, additional compliance controls are needed.
mitigations: Disable telemetry if not needed.
Keep regulated data out of Haystack prompts.
Document retention for any logs containing usage stats.
requires-engineering: add a data-class policy for cross-agent flows.
